zh.title: 民航局舉辦無人機與先進空中交通論壇，將持續推動跨國認證
zh.summary: 交通部民航局11月23日舉辦國際無人機及先進空中交通論壇，吸引近160位產官學界代表。民航局表示，將透過測試空域、檢驗制度與跨國合作，協助國內業者接軌國際標準。
body: 交通部民用航空局11月23日舉辦2026國際無人機及先進空中交通論壇，邀請航空監理、適航檢定與安全標準專家分享實務，近160位國內產官學界代表參與。議程包括美國的無人機及先進空中交通檢驗政策，以及電動垂直起降航空器的安全評估。
民航局長何淑萍表示，截至2026年6月底，臺灣登記的無人機已超過4萬2千架，累計核准的飛航活動超過3萬件。民航局已整合測試空域供業者驗證技術，並將繼續推動跨國雙邊認證，改善飛航活動申請與檢驗程序。
民航局指出，先進空中交通若要進入實際營運，仍須建立適航認證、安全監理與空域整合機制。民航局將從完善檢驗標準、讓檢驗技術與國際接軌，以及擴大國際合作三方面推動後續工作。

en.title: Taiwan aviation regulator holds drone forum and seeks closer certification cooperation
en.summary: Taiwan’s Civil Aviation Administration held a drone and advanced air mobility forum on Nov. 23, drawing nearly 160 participants. The agency said it would use test airspace, updated inspection procedures and cross-border cooperation to help local developers meet international standards.
body: Taiwan’s Civil Aviation Administration held its International Drone and Advanced Air Mobility Forum on Nov. 23. Nearly 160 participants from industry, government and academia attended. Speakers discussed U.S. inspection policies for drones and advanced air mobility and how to assess the safety of electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft.

CAA Director General Shu-ping Ho said Taiwan had registered more than 42,000 drones and approved more than 30,000 flight activities by the end of June 2026. She said the agency has coordinated test airspace for developers and will continue pursuing bilateral certification cooperation and improving its flight application and inspection procedures.

The CAA said bringing advanced air mobility into service would require airworthiness certification, safety oversight and a framework for integrating the aircraft into shared airspace. The agency said its next steps include refining inspection standards, aligning inspection methods with international practice and expanding cooperation overseas.

facts.claim: The CAA held the forum on Nov. 23 and reported nearly 160 attendees.
The forum covered U.S. inspection policy and safety assessment for electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft.
The CAA reported more than 42,000 registered drones and 30,000 or more approved flight activities by the end of June 2026.
The CAA has coordinated test airspace and plans to continue bilateral certification cooperation and improve application and inspection procedures.
The agency identified airworthiness certification, safety oversight and airspace integration as prerequisites for advanced air mobility operations.
